Corporate.brandDescription: Wyatt Financial Holdings operates a portfolio of financial services brands across banking, insurance, wealth management, and lending categories.
Corporate.scope:
Wyatt Financial Holdings works across:
• Multi-brand financial services operations
• Shared regulatory compliance across federal and state jurisdictions
• Shared technology infrastructure and core banking
• Capital markets and treasury operations
• Annual investor and operator reporting
Corporate.mission: To provide a serious operating platform for mid-tier financial services brands that want to keep their identity and outsource the operations.
Corporate.vision: A financial services operator whose portfolio brands grow under their own names because the regulatory and capital infrastructure are shared.
coreValues: Senior — partners deal with partners.
Operational — regulatory compliance runs on schedule.
Reliable — predictable capital and technology infrastructure across brands.
Discreet — brand and regulatory relationships stay private.
Corporate.brandNameRationale: Wyatt is a real American surname with a heritage financial-services register. Financial Holdings follows the multi-brand operator naming convention used in financial services (PNC Financial Services, Truist Financial, Citizens Financial Group structure). The pair reads as an institutional operator with multi-brand portfolio scale.
Corporate.manifesto: Wyatt Financial Holdings owns and operates a portfolio of financial services brands across banking, insurance, wealth management, and lending. Each brand retains its identity, customer relationships, and product roadmap; we operate the shared regulatory compliance, technology infrastructure, and capital markets operations. The buyer is a brand founder considering sale, a regulator-supervised entity seeking consolidated relationships, or an institutional investor holding financial-services assets.
Corporate.industrySummary: Financial services has consolidated under a small number of large multi-brand holding companies (Wells Fargo, PNC, Truist, Citizens Financial). The opening underneath is for a regional mid-tier multi-brand operator with deep regulatory operations and the procurement-grade reliability institutional investors and regulators require.
Corporate.competitorLandscape: Truist Financial (truist.com) is the multi-brand mid-tier financial reference. Citizens Financial Group (citizensbank.com) holds the multi-brand peer slot. Regions Financial (regions.com) sits in the regional multi-brand peer position. KeyCorp (key.com) plays the multi-brand financial peer reference. We belong in the regional mid-tier multi-brand financial-services holding category.
Corporate.positioningStatement: Wyatt Financial Holdings is a regional multi-brand financial services operator running shared regulatory compliance, technology infrastructure, and capital markets operations across a portfolio of brands.
Corporate.positioningRationale: We compete on shared regulatory infrastructure, technology depth, and the procurement-grade reliability brand founders and institutional investors need in a regulated industry.

targetAudience.primary: Financial services brand founders considering sale, regulator-supervised entities seeking consolidated holding relationships, and institutional investors holding financial-services assets.
behaviors: Manage multi-brand financial-services operations.
Negotiate multi-year regulatory and technology agreements.
Care about regulatory compliance, capital adequacy, and operational risk.
Renew on multi-year operating terms.
motivations: Need an operator with shared regulatory infrastructure.
Need to keep brand identity post-acquisition.
Need a single-vendor multi-brand financial-services relationship.

dos: Lead with brand portfolio, regulatory record, and capital adequacy ratios.
Speak the language of brand founders, regulators, and institutional investors.
Publish quarterly operator letters.
Refer to brands by name, not by Wyatt tagging.
donts: No social media at the parent level.
No brand consolidation announcements without partner alignment.

Creative.brandNameRationale: Float is the real banking term for money in transit between accounts. The definite article + Co suffix follows the considered-creative trade-name school.
Creative.manifesto: Most fintech brands are quiet, clean, and slightly boring. We respect that. But there's a customer who wants their money app to have a personality. Someone who treats their finances seriously but talks about them with humor. We made Bank Shot for them.
Creative.industrySummary: Consumer fintech is dominated by sleek, monochrome, slightly cold apps. There's room for one that's warm, witty, and still serious about helping people handle their money. The category has been cold for too long.
Creative.competitorLandscape: Cash App (cash.app) figured out cultural relevance. Step (step.com) is the closest in playful tone. Cleo (cleo-ai.com) leans hard into personality. Albert (albert.com) had the tone for a moment. We're sharper and older in tone than any of them.

Creative.tagline: A fintech brand for the money you put away.
Creative.brandDescription: The Side Pocket Co is a creative-led fintech brand specializing in dedicated savings buckets — 'side pockets' — for specific upcoming expenses and goals, with no general-purpose checking or investment products.
Creative.scope:
The Side Pocket Co works across:
• Dedicated savings buckets ('side pockets') for specific expenses and goals
• Plain published interest on each side pocket
• Automatic allocation rules from connected primary accounts
• Quarterly published essays on personal savings practice
• Annual side-pocket recap sent to customers
Creative.mission: To restore the practice of putting money aside for specific things.
Creative.vision: A fintech brand whose side-pocket model becomes a standard reference for personal savings practice.
coreValues: Warm — the side pocket is for what matters to the customer.
Specific — every pocket has a name.
Considered — savings practice is the work.
Literary — the writing about savings is part of the brand.
Creative.brandNameRationale: Side Pocket is the real financial-trade phrase for a separately-managed allocation within a broader fund (originating in hedge-fund terminology and extended to personal-finance usage). The definite article + Co suffix follows the considered-creative trade-name school. The brand stakes a clear creative position around dedicated savings buckets as a practice.
Creative.manifesto: Most modern banking treats savings as one general pool. We started The Side Pocket Co because the actual practice of putting money aside works better when each bucket has a name — the car repair fund, the trip fund, the holiday fund, the emergency fund. The app is built around those side pockets. Each one has a name, a target, and a published interest rate.
Creative.industrySummary: Personal savings products have converged on general savings accounts. There is real space for a creative-led fintech that positions explicitly on dedicated bucket savings — closer to the envelope budgeting tradition than to modern general-purpose banking.
Creative.competitorLandscape: Qapital (qapital.com) plays the closest peer in goal-based savings. Digit (formerly digit.co, now Oportun) holds the automated-savings peer slot. Acorns (acorns.com) sits in the micro-savings peer position. Ally Buckets (ally.com) plays the bucket-savings feature reference. We sit alongside Qapital with a sharper side-pocket creative position.
Creative.positioningStatement: The Side Pocket Co is a fintech brand specializing in dedicated savings buckets for specific expenses and goals, with plain published interest on each bucket.
Creative.positioningRationale: The brand competes on the bucket-savings premise. Every product, every feature, and every essay is built around the side-pocket practice.

targetAudience.primary: Adults 28-50 who save toward multiple specific goals and want savings buckets rather than a general savings pool.
behaviors: Save toward specific upcoming expenses (car repair, holiday, trip).
Use envelope-budgeting methods or want to.
Care about transparent interest on savings.
Subscribe to recurring services for specific needs.
motivations: Want dedicated savings buckets with names and targets.
Want plain published interest on each bucket.
Want a brand built around the savings practice.

dos: Lead with the side-pocket practice and the published interest rates.
Publish the quarterly essay on personal savings practice.
Show actual side-pocket structures in marketing.
Sign correspondence by the head of customer relations.
donts: No tier system based on balance.

messagingPillars.description: Each side pocket earns published variable interest. The rates are updated monthly and shown per pocket.

messagingPillars.name: Quarterly essay
messagingPillars.description: The brand publishes a long-form essay on personal savings practice every quarter — history, tradition, customer stories. The essay is the brand's primary marketing artefact.
